summary: Correct the immutable-branch review's 34 findings and the associated recovery, authority-capacity, CI lifecycle and evidence defects without promoting a phase gate.

guide.reason: Operator-visible disk refusal, Erase/Repair navigation, update/control retries, replacement recovery, version ordering and publication recovery instructions changed. The guide distinguishes Core recovery from cached Controller tasks and states native/simulated verification limits.

api.reason: Existing pool-update operations, authenticated managed inventory and signed update_rollout authority now expose normalized durable control receipts, replication_pending, reserved_result_bytes and rollback_started, with replay/conflict/pending/capacity errors and Core-owned continuation. Both producer/consumer sides, local/client/peer schemas and generated references are updated; older typed Core peers cannot acknowledge unknown signed fields, requiring the documented coordinated Core upgrade. No new endpoint is added. Image arm/cancel/reboot and replacement changes correct existing contracts; offline installers, publishing/build tools and lab safety add no Controller/Core endpoint.

roadmap.reason: Bug corrections do not promote any milestone or phase acceptance. Existing physical, firmware, lab, live-forge and redistribution gates remain open; plan notes only record this correction scope and API/state decision.

state.reason: Core executes/reconciles updates and owns accepted pool control identities, outcomes, pending rollback and capacity reservations. Controller adds no pool table, cache, mapping or scheduler; it only presents host results and reconciles the existing authenticated operation audit record.
state.record: The pool master's agent data-directory pool-update.json retains normalized control receipts with original outcomes. Its signed update_rollout section is retained in members' pool-replica.json and adopted by the promoted Core master with the same request and rollout identities. A fresh/replaced Controller obtains Inventory.managed.update_rollout through authenticated host inventory; it does not need the former Controller database to recover pool history. Existing Core update/swap journals retain arm/checkpoint intent; build/publisher/lab fixtures do not introduce Controller-owned pool state.

verification.method: Executed changed Go packages and targeted race checks; web typecheck, behavior checks/build and actual Chromium interaction with a simulated API; actual text wizard with controlled debconf/tools; native scratch CLI disk-alias refusal, release ordering and native CI smokes; API/documentation checks. The isolated-source combined Python run passed 342 tests before the final two-file CI owned-session correction; all 56 focused CI/version/security checks and the actual native wrapper passed afterward, with independent re-review. Other Python sources were unchanged; the entire combined run was not repeated after that correction. The initial empty-output startup failure's cause remains unproven. The existing privacy scanner found no findings in all 92 assessed paths; full-root privacy is blocked by 14 unrelated pre-existing indexed wrapper-shell dumps, restored unchanged. No history cleanup is claimed. The QA report records commands, results and physical/live-forge limits.
